input.summary: H1 flat 2 is already lit: measured in its own storey (rooms-build.json, file y 19 = world y 14), min 9, mean 11.9, 0 dark, 0 dim, 146/146 floor cells reachable. Added no lamps, because the designer's two dim east corners do not exist at this storey and the rule is no more lamps than needed.
left: The designer's request (a lantern for the two dim east corners) is not applied: those corners were a measurement artifact. `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` reads world y as file y, so it measured the flat 1 storey (file y 14..17 = world y 9..12) and reported it as 'H1 flat 2'. Ask the designer to re-check against rooms-build.json if they still want the extra lantern.

H1 flat 1 (flat 1 storey, world y 9..12, box 26,14,9,36,17,23 in the file frame) is genuinely dark-dim: min 3, mean 8.2, 48 dim cells, 0 dark, and its lantern spots are 32,14,21 (lifts 36 cells), 26,14,12 (9 cells) and 26,14,9 (1 cell). That belongs to the flat 1 lamplighter, and parts/room-2.mjs placed 0 blocks in the build log, so check whether flat 1's furniture part exists before lighting it.

No edits to parts/room-3.mjs or any other module: the lamps already in the build (parts/lights.mjs flat-2 hangs at y 17, plus room-3's H and L rows) light the storey fully, so I left the designer's furniture and lanterns untouched. make.sh ran cleanly and rebuilt build.nbt (15089 blocks), and the parts report shows 0 refused writes.

waste.what: Measured the wrong storey for a long stretch: `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` silently treats world y as file y, so 'H1 flat 2' showed dim corners that were really flat 1's floor (world y 9). I only caught it by comparing against rooms-build.json.
waste.cost: about 4 room runs, plus a second read of the rooms and floor maps, before the frame mismatch was clear
waste.tool: mcd room / mcd light / mcd plan should refuse or warn when the rooms file's y range does not match the file's frame (or auto-read rooms-build.json beside build.nbt). The build.mjs comment already says rooms-build.json is the file-frame version, so the lamplighter prompt should name it too.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which corner cells were dim from the light grid, reading each row's characters against x (x=26 is the first column, and '#' cells are skipped).
waste.tool: mcd light --json or a 'list cells below N' option (e.g. --below 8 --room X) would give the dim cells and their coordinates directly

companions.task: Light flat 1 of H1 (the storey the wrong-frame measure showed dim) once its furniture part exists: its own lantern spots from `mcd room ... rooms-build.json --only "H1 flat 1"`.
Confirm the H1 flat 2 furniture needs no change and that the east-corner lantern request was made against the flat 1 storey; the designer owns the furniture and the lane cells.

left: The designer's request (a lantern for the two dim east corners) is not applied: those corners were a measurement artifact. `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` reads world y as file y, so it measured the flat 1 storey (file y 14..17 = world y 9..12) and reported it as 'H1 flat 2'. Ask the designer to re-check against rooms-build.json if they still want the extra lantern.

H1 flat 1 (flat 1 storey, world y 9..12, box 26,14,9,36,17,23 in the file frame) is genuinely dark-dim: min 3, mean 8.2, 48 dim cells, 0 dark, and its lantern spots are 32,14,21 (lifts 36 cells), 26,14,12 (9 cells) and 26,14,9 (1 cell). That belongs to the flat 1 lamplighter, and parts/room-2.mjs placed 0 blocks in the build log, so check whether flat 1's furniture part exists before lighting it.

No edits to parts/room-3.mjs or any other module: the lamps already in the build (parts/lights.mjs flat-2 hangs at y 17, plus room-3's H and L rows) light the storey fully, so I left the designer's furniture and lanterns untouched. make.sh ran cleanly and rebuilt build.nbt (15089 blocks), and the parts report shows 0 refused writes.

waste.what: Measured the wrong storey for a long stretch: `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` silently treats world y as file y, so 'H1 flat 2' showed dim corners that were really flat 1's floor (world y 9). I only caught it by comparing against rooms-build.json.
waste.cost: about 4 room runs, plus a second read of the rooms and floor maps, before the frame mismatch was clear
waste.tool: mcd room / mcd light / mcd plan should refuse or warn when the rooms file's y range does not match the file's frame (or auto-read rooms-build.json beside build.nbt). The build.mjs comment already says rooms-build.json is the file-frame version, so the lamplighter prompt should name it too.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which corner cells were dim from the light grid, reading each row's characters against x (x=26 is the first column, and '#' cells are skipped).
waste.tool: mcd light --json or a 'list cells below N' option (e.g. --below 8 --room X) would give the dim cells and their coordinates directly

companions.task: Light flat 1 of H1 (the storey the wrong-frame measure showed dim) once its furniture part exists: its own lantern spots from `mcd room ... rooms-build.json --only "H1 flat 1"`.
Confirm the H1 flat 2 furniture needs no change and that the east-corner lantern request was made against the flat 1 storey; the designer owns the furniture and the lane cells.
